text.setup: Bar on your upper back, hands just outside your shoulders. Feet about shoulder-width, toes out 15–30°. Big breath and brace before every rep.
cues: Break at the hips and knees together and sit down between your heels.
Knees travel out over your toes; keep the bar over the middle of your foot.
Full depth is the hip crease below the top of the knee — then drive up, chest and hips rising together.
mistakes: Hips shooting up first, so the squat turns into a good morning.
Heels lifting off the floor.
Knees caving in on the way up.
Losing the brace at the bottom.

variants.barbell: Set the safety arms just below your bottom position before the first set.
variants.smith: The bar runs on a fixed track, so your feet can sit a little further forward than a free squat.
variants.safety_squat_bar: Hold the handles in front. The cambered bar sits further forward and tips you into the hole, so fight to stay upright.
variants.belt_squat: The load hangs from a belt at your hips, so your back carries nothing. Stay tall and sit straight down.
variants.dumbbells: Hold one dumbbell upright against your chest, elbows pointing down inside your knees.
variants.kettlebell: Hold the bell by the horns against your chest, elbows pointing down inside your knees.

text.setup: Bar over the middle of your foot, about a fist from your shins. Hips-width stance. Grip just outside your legs, then bring your shins to the bar.
cues: Chest up, lats tight — pull the slack out of the bar until it clicks against the plates.
Push the floor away; the bar stays in contact with your legs the whole way.
Finish by squeezing your hips through. Stand tall, don't lean back.
mistakes: Hips rising before the bar leaves the floor.
The bar drifting forward away from the legs.
Jerking the bar off the floor instead of squeezing it.

variants.barbell: Mixed grip or hook grip for heavy sets; straps are fine for back work.
variants.trap_bar: Handles at your sides, so you can sit lower and use more leg. High handles shorten the pull.
variants.smith: The fixed track removes the balance part — keep your shins close anyway.
variants.axle: The thick bar doesn't rotate and is hard to hold; double overhand or a hook grip, no straps in most comps.
variants.dumbbells: Bells at your sides or just in front of your thighs; same hinge, lighter load.
variants.kettlebell: One bell between your feet, gripped with both hands.

labels: Shoulder blades back, feet down, brace
Press up and back over your shoulders

text.setup: Eyes under the bar. Squeeze your shoulder blades back and down, feet planted, slight arch. Grip so your forearms are vertical at the bottom.
cues: Unrack with straight arms and bring the bar over your shoulders.
Lower it under control to your lower chest, elbows about 45° from your body.
Press up and slightly back so it finishes over your shoulders again.
mistakes: Shoulder blades coming apart off the bench.
Elbows flaring straight out to the sides.
Bouncing the bar off your chest.

variants.barbell: Use a spotter or set the safety arms just below chest height.
variants.smith: The track is fixed, so the bar can't follow its natural curve — set the bench so it touches just below your nipples.
variants.dumbbells: Each arm works on its own and you can go a little deeper. Bring the bells down to the sides of your chest.
variants.machine: Set the seat so the handles line up with the middle of your chest.
variants.plate_loaded_machine: Set the seat so the handles line up with the middle of your chest.

labels: Bar on your front delts, brace
Press — head back out of the way

text.setup: Bar resting on your front delts, hands just outside your shoulders, forearms vertical. Feet hip-width, glutes and abs tight.
cues: Press straight up and pull your chin back so the bar clears your face.
Once it passes your forehead, push your head through between your arms.
Lock out with the bar over the middle of your foot.
mistakes: Leaning back to turn it into a standing incline press.
Pressing the bar around your face instead of moving your head.
Losing tension in the glutes and abs.

variants.barbell: Start from a rack set at about collarbone height.
variants.smith: The track sets the bar path, so step slightly forward of it to clear your face.
variants.dumbbells: Start with the bells at shoulder height, palms forward or facing in. Each side has to stay stable on its own.
variants.kettlebell: The bell sits in the rack against your forearm; press with your wrist straight.
variants.machine: Set the seat so the handles start level with your shoulders.
variants.axle: Clean it to your chest first — the thick bar rolls, so keep your wrists stacked.

labels: Hinge over, flat back, arms long

text.setup: Hinge forward to roughly 45° or lower with soft knees and a flat back. Let your arms hang straight.
cues: Pull your elbows back past your torso, not up towards your ears.
Bring the bar to your lower ribs and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Lower all the way to straight arms without letting your back round.
mistakes: Standing up more each rep to cheat the weight up.
Rounding the lower back.
Shrugging instead of pulling with the back.

variants.barbell: Overhand grip works more upper back, underhand a little more lats.
variants.dumbbells: One hand and knee on a bench for support, or both bells with your chest down.
variants.cable: A low cable keeps tension at the bottom where a free weight goes slack.
variants.smith: The fixed track means you have to set your body to the bar, not the other way round.

labels: Pull your elbows down to your sides

text.setup: Sit with your knees snug under the pads and grip a little wider than shoulder-width. Lean back slightly, chest up.
cues: Start the pull by bringing your shoulder blades down.
Drive your elbows down to your sides.
Touch the bar to your upper chest, then let your arms go long again.
mistakes: Leaning way back and turning it into a row.
Pulling the bar behind your neck.
Letting the stack slam between reps.

variants.cable: A wide bar works the lats through more range; a close neutral handle lets you pull further.
variants.machine: Set the seat so you can just reach the handles with straight arms.
variants.plate_loaded_machine: Set the seat so you can just reach the handles with straight arms.

text.setup: Stand tall with a bell in each hand at your sides, a small bend in the elbows, a slight lean forward.
cues: Raise your arms out to the sides, leading with your elbows.
Stop at about shoulder height — hands level with or just below your elbows.
Lower slowly; don't let the bells fall.
mistakes: Swinging the body to get the weight up.
Shrugging the shoulders up to your ears.
Going too heavy and turning it into an upright row.

variants.dumbbells: Light is right: the lever is long, so small weights feel heavy.
variants.cable: One arm at a time from a low pulley on the opposite side; tension stays on at the bottom.
variants.machine: Pads sit against the outside of your arms — push with the elbows, not the hands.
variants.resistance_band: Stand on the band; it gets harder the higher you go, so pick a light one.

labels: Stand tall, elbows by your sides

text.setup: Stand tall, feet hip-width, elbows by your sides. Grip about shoulder-width.
cues: Curl the weight up by bending only at the elbows.
Keep your elbows from drifting forward as you near the top.
Lower all the way to straight arms, slower than you lifted.
mistakes: Swinging with the hips and back.
Elbows riding forward to cheat the top.
Stopping short of straight arms at the bottom.

variants.barbell: An EZ bar is kinder to the wrists than a straight bar.
variants.dumbbells: Turn your palms up as you curl to get the most from the biceps.
variants.cable: Tension stays on all the way down, unlike a free weight.
variants.machine: Line your elbows up with the machine's pivot.
variants.kettlebell: The bell hangs below the handle, so it's hardest near the top.
variants.resistance_band: Stand on the band; it gets harder the higher you curl.

labels: Let it come back up to chest height

text.setup: Face the cable stack, hinge forward a little, elbows pinned to your sides.
cues: Push down until your arms are straight.
Only your forearms move; your upper arms stay put.
Let it come back up to about chest height under control.
mistakes: Elbows flaring out or swinging forward.
Leaning over the handle and pushing with body weight.
Cutting the range short at the top.

variants.cable: A rope lets you spread your hands at the bottom; a straight bar lets you go heavier.
variants.machine: Set the seat so your elbows sit on the pad and line up with the pivot.
variants.resistance_band: Anchor the band high; it's hardest at lockout.

labels: Drop your back knee straight down
Drive up through your front foot

text.setup: Take a long stance — front foot flat, back foot on its toes, hips square. Stand tall.
cues: Drop your back knee straight down towards the floor.
Front shin stays fairly upright; front heel stays down.
Drive up through your whole front foot.
mistakes: A stance so short the front knee shoots forward and the heel lifts.
Feet on one line, like a tightrope, so you wobble.
Leaning the torso forward and pushing off the back leg.

variants.dumbbells: Bells at your sides make balance easier than a bar.
variants.barbell: Set up in a rack with safety arms; balance is harder with the load high on your back.
variants.smith: The track handles the balance, so you can focus on the legs.
variants.kettlebell: Hold bells at your sides, or one at your chest.
variants.safety_squat_bar: The handles let you hold the rack for balance if you need it.
variants.bodyweight: Hands on hips; the first step is getting the balance right.
